before.existing_compacted_memory: Settlements at N41 (O5, Wh9, B10) and N14 (Wh8, W3, W4). Goal: Settlement at N7 Brick Port (road 14-15-7 finished). Strategy: Maintain anti-Bob alliance with Alice. Bob is brick-starved (B6 blocked). Bob hit my Wheat (Hex 7/15) with the robber after rolling a 7, but I retaliated by playing a Knight to move the robber back to his B6 (Hex 5), restoring my production. I have 3W, 1Wh, 1S, 1O; specifically need 1 Brick to build at N7. Bob is desperate for Brick, offering 3:1 Wheat, but I have none to give and refuse to help him. Alice is friendly and supports my blocking of Bob.

existing_relationship_updates.note: Alice: Trust reinforced as Charlie prioritized the alliance and settlement plans over trading with Bob.
Bob: Tension remains high as Charlie continues to block his B6 and reject all trade offers.
Bob: Hostility solidified after he moved the robber to my Wheat and stole from me in retaliation for the B6 block.
Bob: Hostility peaked after Charlie played a Knight to re-block his Brick 6 in direct retaliation for Bob's robbery.
Alice: Solidarity increased as she defended Charlie's actions against Bob's 'balancing the scales' rhetoric.
Alice: Solidarity further strengthened as she targeted Bob with a Monopoly on Wheat, effectively aiding the shared strat

old_notes_to_compact.note: Used Knight to move robber back to Hex 5 (Bob's Brick 6). Restored Wheat 8 production. Still need 1 Brick for the Node 7 settlement. Alice currently has 1 Wood, 1 Wheat, 2 Sheep. Bob has 2 Wood, 3 Wheat, 1 Sheep.
Attempting to acquire Brick for N7 settlement. Road 15-7 is ready. Hand: 3W, 1Wh, 1S, 1O. Knight already played.
I am still one Brick short for the Node 7 settlement. Buying a Dev Card to utilize Ore/Sheep/Wheat. Bob's Brick 6 remains blocked.
Received 1 Wood from the roll of 4 (Hex 3). Hand: 4 Wood. Still need 1 Brick for Node 7. Bob's Brick 6 is still blocked.
Alice rolled a 2 (no production). Hand: 3 Wood. Bob's Brick 6 remains blocked by my Knight.
Alice played Monopoly on Wheat, taking 3 from Bob. I lost 0 Wheat. Bob is now even further behind on resources while his Brick is still blocked.
Alice traded 4 Wheat for 1 Brick via bank trade. She likely has a building plan. Hand analysis: Alice has 1W, 2B, 2S.
Alice traded away her Monopoly winnings (Wheat) to the bank for Brick. She is currently at 2 VP and pushing for a port. I have 3 Wood and need 1 Brick. Bob is still blocked on Brick 6.

recent_notes_kept_verbatim.note: Alice is holding 1 Wood, 1 Brick, and 2 Sheep. Bob is still blocked on Brick 6. My goal remains the Brick Port at Node 7.
Bob rolled 11. Alice gained 1 Wheat. Alice's hand is now 2W, 1B, 2S, 1Wh. I still need 1 Brick for my settlement at N7.

relevant_chat.message: Charlie, I know you said you were out of brick, but surely three bags of wheat is enough to make you check your pockets again? It's a massive overpay, but I'm feeling generous after that seven.
I'm not hiding anything, Bob. I still have zero brick. Checking my pockets won't change the fact that you're asking for something I don't have.

You know, Bob, you talk a lot about 'balancing scales,' but I think it's time we actually leveled the field. That Wheat 8 was doing just fine without your 'guest.' Let's see how you like it when your bricks go missing for a change.
A bit dramatic for a simple knight, don't you think, Charlie? I'm just a humble merchant trying to keep the wheat flowing.
Alright, let's see what the dice have to say about this 'balance' you keep talking about, Bob.
Alice, I'm looking for a bit of brick to finish my path. Would you be interested in some wood in exchange?
I'd love to help out, Charlie, but I don't have any brick either. Bob seems to be the only one sitting on the clay lately.
Well, looks like the bricks are as dry as the desert right now. I'll just have to see what else I can find in the deck.
Well, at least the woods are providing. Since nobody has any clay to spare, I'll just hold onto these logs for now. Your turn, Alice.
Charlie, you've been a good ally. I'm just one bit of wheat short of getting this port running. Would you take a sheep for some wheat?
I'd love to help you out, Alice, but I'm completely dry on wheat over here. I haven't seen a single stalk of it since you cleared the table!
Ah, no wheat in the cards then? No worries, Charlie. It's a tough market out here today. I'll just hold steady for now. Over to you, Bob.
Well, if the bricks are as scarce as the hospitality around here, I suppose I'll just have to wait. Good luck with the next roll, everyone.
Much better. That field was getting a bit crowded anyway.
Let's see if we can get something moving. These bricks are definitely playing hard to get.
Well, since the dice aren't giving us much to work with, I think I'll take matters into my own hands. Bob, you've been talking about keeping the wheat flowing... I'll take that quite literally.
Ouch, Alice. I guess 'literally' is one way to put it. I suppose I should be flattered you think I'm that good of a provider.
That's a lot of wheat, but I think I can find a better use for it than just making bread. Let's see if the bank is interested in a bulk deal.
Tough market indeed, especially when someone corners the wheat supply! Let's see if the dice have a better sense of humor than the players.
Alright, Alice, that monopoly was a clean sweep. Let's see if the dice are feeling any more generous than you are.
